questions.question: How does remember find the same stored value on the next recomposition?
options: By the name of the variable it is assigned to
By hashing the value returned from the lambda
By the call's position in the group structure
By a unique ID the developer must pass in on every single call
questions.explanation: This is positional memoization: the value is stored in the slot table at the position of the call, inside groups keyed by source location. On recomposition the same call site reaches the same slot. Variable names don't exist at runtime, and keys are optional extras, not the base mechanism.

questions.question: The slot table stores groups and remembered values in flat arrays organised as a gap buffer, which makes inserting near the current position cheap.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The slot table is a gap buffer: a flat array with a movable empty region. Composition walks it in order, so inserts usually happen at the current spot and only require moving the gap. Moving the gap far away is costly, which is fine because UI changes tend to be local.

questions.question: `show` flips from false to true. What happens to `count`?
options: It resets to 0 because Header now takes the slot it used to occupy
It keeps its value, as the if branch is wrapped in its own group
It throws, since the slot table detects a changed number of calls
It keeps its value, but only if Header is marked @Stable or @Immutable
questions.explanation: The compiler wraps the if body in its own group, so turning it on inserts a group at that spot without shifting the identity of the code after it. The remember below keeps matching its old slot. Stability affects skipping, not slot identity.

questions.question: Each ItemRow remembers its own `expanded` flag. A new item is inserted at the top of `items`. What happens to the expanded state?
options: State follows each item correctly because Item is a data class
All rows lose their remembered state and start out collapsed again
State stays at each index, so rows show their neighbour's state
Compose throws because the number of loop iterations changed
questions.explanation: Without keys, loop iterations are matched by position, so the remembered state at index 0 now belongs to the new item and everything is shifted by one. Wrapping the body in key(item.id) lets the runtime match groups by identity and move state with the item.

questions.question: Which statements about the key() composable and lazy item keys are true? Select all that apply.
options: key(id) lets the runtime match groups by identity, so state moves when items reorder
key() makes its content skip recomposition while the key value is unchanged
Changing the value passed to key() at a call site resets the state remembered inside
LazyColumn item keys must be unique; a duplicate key throws at runtime
Values passed to key() are saved across process death automatically
questions.explanation: key() gives a group an identity beyond its position: same key means same group (even if moved), a new key means a new group with fresh state. LazyColumn needs unique keys and crashes on duplicates. key() has nothing to do with skipping, and it doesn't save anything to a Bundle.

questions.question: `items` is an ArrayList that is mutated in place (add/remove) and then the composable recomposes with the same list. What does `sorted` hold?
options: A freshly sorted copy, because remember deep-compares lists
A stale result, as the key is the same instance and so equal
A freshly sorted copy, because mutation changes the list's hashCode
It throws, since mutable collections can't be remember keys
questions.explanation: remember stores the key and compares the new one with the old one using equals. Here both are the same object, so they're trivially equal and the lambda isn't re-run, leaving a stale result. Use immutable lists (a new instance per change) or snapshot state such as mutableStateListOf.

questions.question: Values stored with plain remember survive a configuration change such as rotation, as long as the Activity doesn't declare configChanges.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Rotation recreates the Activity, which builds a brand-new composition and slot table, so remembered values are gone. rememberSaveable (via saved instance state) or a ViewModel is needed to keep them. remember only survives recomposition within the same composition.

questions.question: A video player composable must move between a Column in portrait and a Row in landscape (the Activity handles configChanges) without losing its remembered state. What is the right tool?
options: Wrap the player in key("player") in both layouts
Store all of the player's state in rememberSaveable
Create it with movableContentOf and use it in both
Provide the player through a CompositionLocalProvider
questions.explanation: movableContentOf lets a chunk of composition, with its slot table groups and remembered state, be moved to a different place in the tree. key() only matches groups among siblings under the same parent, so moving to a different parent still loses state. rememberSaveable would save values but rebuild the player.

questions.question: An object implementing RememberObserver is stored with remember. Which statements are true? Select all that apply.
options: onRemembered is called as soon as the remember lambda returns, during composition
onForgotten is called when the call leaves the composition or its keys change
onAbandoned is called if the composition is discarded before it is applied
onRemembered is called once the composition holding it has been applied
questions.explanation: Callbacks follow the composition's commit: onRemembered fires after apply, not while the lambda runs, because the composition might still be thrown away. If it is, the object gets onAbandoned instead. onForgotten fires when it leaves, and this is how DisposableEffect and LaunchedEffect are built.

questions.question: A composable inside `if (show)` uses remember. `show` goes false and then true again. What happens to the remembered value?
options: It is restored, because the slot table keeps hidden groups around
It is recomputed, since the group was removed with the branch
It is restored, but only if the remembered value is a State object
It stays in memory but the composable can't read it any more
questions.explanation: When the branch leaves, its group and slots are removed from the slot table and the values are forgotten. Coming back inserts a new group, so remember runs its lambda again. To keep state across this, hoist it above the if or use rememberSaveable.
